title: Payloads with explicit null error are marked as failures
reasoning: ToolResult.from_payload infers success from the presence of the error key, not from whether the error value is meaningful. A mapping-shaped tool payload that includes a stable field set such as {"error": null, "data": ...} will be normalized with success=false even though there is no error. That can make successful SDK/local-runtime ingress results look failed whenever callers include nullable error fields for schema stability.
reproduction: Call ToolResult.from_payload({"error": None, "data": {"output": "ok"}}); the returned ToolResult has success=False.
recommendation: Infer success from a truthy/non-empty error value when success is absent, for example kwargs["success"] = not bool(result_payload.get("error")), while preserving explicit success values.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and the edge case requires a payload that includes an explicit nullable error field while omitting success.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for ToolResult.from_payload with {"error": None, "data": {"output": "ok"}} asserting success is True and llm_content is "ok", plus a non-empty error case asserting success is False.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/core/interfaces/tool.py and a focused backend unit test for ToolResult.from_payload normalization.
